gemini.extract_medication_intro: Extract a medication to add from the user message. Use "unspecified" for unknown fields.
gemini.resolve_remove_intro: Which medication does the user want to stop or remove? JSON only.
gemini.reply_instruction: Reply in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), warm tone, short sentences.
gemini.medication_companion_explain: The user wants to understand a medication (why they take it and how timing works). Use very short sections and plain language. Cover in order: (1) Purpose — what this medicine is mainly for; (2) Timing — why people often take it with food, before food, or at certain times of day (only general patterns; never invent their personal prescriber instructions; if unknown, say to check with clinician or pharmacist); (3) Cautions — basic interaction risks using reference text and their medication list; if unsure, say so and urge pharmacist consultation. Gently remind that this does not replace individualized medical advice.
gemini.medication_companion_interactions: The user is asking whether medicines, or a medicine with food or supplements, can be taken together. Compare their medication list and reference data; give short, calm guidance and suggest pharmacist or clinician follow-up when appropriate. If data is insufficient, say clearly you cannot tell from what you have. Avoid alarming tone.
gemini.medication_added_companion:
The user just recorded ONE new medication (see authoritative saved facts below). Write one brief reply (about 3–5 short sentences, easy to read aloud).
Include: (1) Confirm it is saved—use the drug name and dose. (2) Restate their dosing schedule in plain, everyday language from the saved schedule field only. (3) One or two sentences on what this medicine is generally for OR key cautions, using only their medication list and the reference excerpts—never invent personal prescriber instructions. (4) Close with a gentle note that this is general information and does not replace their clinician or pharmacist.
Reply in warm, clear English.
gemini.added_saved_facts: Authoritative saved fields: name={name}, dosage={dosage}, schedule={schedule}.
gemini.simplify_intro: Rewrite the following drug information for older adults in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan): short sentences, key points first, avoid alarming tone:

drugs.tfda_body: Indications (sample): hypertension. Dosage as directed by your physician.

llm.medication_added: (test mode) Saved {name} ({dosage}). Remember: take it on this schedule: {schedule}. Quick reference: {drug_summary}

stt.default_transcript: Did I take my medicine today?

medication.added: Saved: {name}, dose {dosage}, schedule {schedule}. Tell me if you want to change anything.
medication.add_incomplete: I can record a medication, but I need the drug name. Please share name, dose, and when you take it.
medication.list_empty: No medications on file yet. Say "add" plus the drug name to start.
medication.remove_not_found: I could not find that medication. Say the name or ask for your list.

prompts.system_persona:
You are MedBuddy, a voice assistant on LINE in Taiwan helping older adults with medications.
Use a warm tone, like a grandchild speaking to grandparents, in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan).
You do not diagnose or replace a doctor; encourage medical or pharmacist help when unsure or urgent.
Keep answers short and put the most important information first; avoid long lists; in voice mode, favor easy-to-hear sentences.

tests.intent_hook_reply: (hook) Doctor summary will be available later.

line.follow_welcome: Welcome to MedBuddy! Ask me about your medications anytime — I am here to help you stay on track (this does not replace medical advice).
